related_resources.reason: Birth, family, law and medicine, Vienna clinic, intervention, teachers, Pest work, family and last illness; institutional biography also corrects the lonely-hero myth.
Chronology and appointments, Vienna teachers, Kolletschka, support, Pest academic role, 1865 death. Austrian institutional view.
Historical series of maternal deaths, comparative clinic design, hypothesis, intervention, patterns after departure; cannot independently reconstruct every ward-level confounder.
Detailed institutional data, clinic divisions, 1847/1848 mortality and interpretation of a natural comparison. Tables were indexed from article.
Reproduces 1846 and 1848 births/deaths for both Vienna clinics. Table checked in search extraction; source is document PDF not image-inspected.
Clinical context and broad timing: chlorine disinfection, 1848 numbers, living-patient transfers and streptococcal disease.
Treats mortality, causal explanation, medical school politics, and argues strongly for injury-based death in asylum. Final causal claims not accepted uncritically.
Reports incomplete early 1847 improvement, carcinoma-associated infections, differing early/1848 mortality and challenge of incomplete early dissemination. An interpretation, not consensus.
Authenticates existence/date/title of Holmes 1843 argument; see history article for specifics.
Scholarly correction that Gordon recognized transmission, advocated preventive measures before Holmes and Semmelweis.
Excerpts from primary comparison, staggered admissions and natural-experiment reasoning.
543-page primary treatise; retrospective and argumentative account of figures and opponents. Wording should be checked against page image for direct quotes.
Original 1861 book, library copy and institutional reception (1862 Hungarian directive).
Bibliographic confirmation of open letters and identified correspondents; no quotations from an uninspected scan.
Wedding portrait, Maria Weidenhofer marriage and children; institutional curator account.
Pest professorship 1855–1865, hospital institutional background and medical-school colleagues.
1857 marriage to Maria Weidenhofer, five children, three reached adulthood. Does not support domestic dialogue.
Hebra and Skoda support; delay in full publication, 1850 presentation and senior clinic opposition.
Predecessors including Gordon, Holmes and nineteenth-century chlorination and asepsis; wider context not a single-person first.
Early notices and correspondence, contested scholarly reception and disease theory.
Records 1861 original and institutional bibliographic dates; direct textual quotations deliberately avoided.
